articles.title: College football just saw the real Lane Kiffin after leaked LSU locker room video from halftime against Clemson goes viral
articles.summary: A lot of "noise" follows LSU head coach Lane Kiffin, but one leaked video of his halftime speech during Saturday's route over Clemson shows a side of Kiffin...
articles.body:
A lot of "noise" follows LSU head coach Lane Kiffin, but one leaked video of his halftime speech during Saturday's route over Clemson shows a side of Kiffin many have never seen before, and may not see again.

If you haven't seen the leaked video of Lane Kiffin's halftime speech against Clemson, you're in for a treat. LSU is clearly the biggest villain in college football , led by a coach many have vilified as the sport's ultimate antagonist . But this video pulls back the curtain on who Kiffin truly is as a head coach, and it tells a very different story than the one most people have been sold .

The halftime speech nobody was supposed to see

Now I'll preface this by saying this is something you're not supposed to see. It's a leaked video from a locker room, but it reveals exactly the type of person Kiffin is and exactly why his players and coaches never have a bad word to say about him. Think about what you typically hear about Lane Kiffin from the outside. The noise, the controversy, the social media antics. It's usually filtered through the media, through other coaches, through contemporaries. But never, or very rarely, do you hear a former player, a coach who worked under him, or somebody who plays for him come out and say they don't like the guy.

Kiffin walked into that locker room with his team up 31-3 at halftime and ripped into them like they were down 31-3. He told them Clemson was soft, that Clemson didn't want to be there, that LSU was the better team, that they'd prepared for the past seven to eight months for this moment, that everybody hates them, that it's them against the world . He used that mentality to lead his team to what became a 40-point victory against a Clemson team that, let's be honest, might be horrible, but still has a lot of NFL talent on that football field.

Coached at premier programs like USC and Tennessee .

Why this could change the narrative around Kiffin

This was a great look for Lane Kiffin - the kind of footage that turns people in his favor. It's the same energy you heard from Kirby Smart at halftime of the national championship when that speech got leaked, the same fire you heard from Nick Saban ahead of his national championship game in 2018. These are the speeches, the sentiments, the words and reactions that fire teams up, that fire fan bases up, that turn tides at programs.

This is exactly why LSU chose Lane Kiffin. Despite all of the noise, all of the nonsense, all of everything that comes with Kiffin as a public figure, he went out and waxed the Clemson Tigers on Saturday night . Say what you want about the theatrics, about him being overly excessive on social media last year, about whatever rubs you the wrong way. When the going gets tough, Lane Kiffin is one of the best coaches in college football.

He showed it in this video. He showed it Saturday night. And he's probably going to show it for the majority of his tenure at LSU.

articles.title: Mics Caught Caitlin Clark's Teammate's Reaction To Her Late 3-Pointer
articles.summary: They caught the reaction online.
articles.body:
Team USA's women's basketball squad improved to 3-0 at the FIBA Women's World Cup on Monday evening.

The American women, led by Breanna Stewart and Napheesa Collier, took down the Czech Republic in blowout fashion on Monday. Team USA looked much better than they did on Sunday. The Americans were coming off a close, 55-52 win over Italy. They rebounded against Czechia with a dominant performance.

Late in the game, Caitlin Clark drilled a 3-pointer from deep. TNT's cameras panned to her teammates on the bench.

Jackie Young was seen clapping on the bench. The veteran WNBA guard was heard telling her teammate, Kahleah Copper: "You better clap."

Of course, there are multiple ways to take this. The Clark supporters will take this as evidence that all of her teammates don't like her.

However, at that stage in the game, when you're leading by more than 40 points, it's reasonable to not clap at every bucket.

Breanna Stewart led the way for Team USA on Monday night, hitting 8 of 11 field goals and scoring 19 points. She was a dominant force.

"I wanted to come out and really lead this team in a number of ways," Stewart said on the broadcast postgame. "Wanted to make sure that today we really took things into our own hands and really lead by example."

The quarterfinals of the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup will begin on Thursday, September 10. There will be quarterfinals qualifications on Tuesday, September 8 and Wednesday, September 9.

Team USA and France are heading into the quarterfinals as the two clear frontrunners to win it all. The Americans and the French could be on a collision course in the gold medal game. It could be a very fun game to watch, with several WNBA stars on display.

Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across MLB. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Diamondbacks fans and fans across the country.

The D-backs have seventeen games left in the season. Perhaps more importantly, they have fourteen games left until the final series of 2026, against the Padres in San Diego. Indications are, that series will likely determine the third wild-card place in the National League post-season. Right now, the D-backs have a one-half game lead over the Padres, with the tiebreaker of the season series to be decided by the winner of the final set at Petco. The other five playoff spots largely seem set, so this is it, as far as excitement goes in the NL. But there are any number of factors that will go into the situation there, and what Arizona needs to do, to reach the post-season.

samath has been particularly keeping a weather eye on this situation, so I'll repost a couple of his comments regarding where things might be, and how we could get there.

There are five possible scenarios assuming no other teams enter the picture from either direction:

Diamondbacks > 3 up on Padres: Moot because they're already in

Diamondbacks 2-3 up on Padres: Just don't get swept

Within a game of each other: Whoever wins the series is in

Padres 2-3 up on Diamondbacks: Sweep to make the playoffs

Paders >3 up on Diamondbacks: Moot because they're already eliminated

Perhaps the most fascinating thing to me: If the two teams are tied entering the game before that series, that final game against the Rockies (and the Padres' game against the Dodgers) will literally not matter whatsoever.

Their remaining schedules are remarkably similar. Both play the Rockies at Coors and the Marlins at home. They each play one very good playoff team — Yankees and Dodgers — and one very bad team — Royals and Giants — leaving the remaining difference comparing the Rangers and Nationals. Three home series left for each. Here's how Fangraphs projects the Diamondbacks' remaining series to go:

Meanwhile, here's how they project the Padres' remaining series to go:

Adding it up, the Padres are projected to be 0.6 games better overall, and they're 0.5 games behind. The projections before the final series are dead even.

Of course, the above are simply "best guesses". It is not, in fact, possible for San Diego to win 1.3 of their 2 remaining games against Washington. It'll be zero, one, or two, impacting how things feel like they will play out down the stretch. But given the above, what do you think will happen over the Diamondbacks' and Padres' remaining games? Will we reach the final series in what's effectively a play-in series? Might the return of Corbin Burnes give the D-backs an edge down the stretch? Or will the struggles of Arizona's offense lead to them playing uphill baseball to the Battle of San Diego? Where will be be after the game of September 24?

That's what the poll below is for, and explain your choice in the comments…

articles.title: Biggest takeaways from the Panthers' first 2026 regular-season depth chart
articles.summary: The Panthers' first depth chart of the 2026 regular season included a few intriguing placements.
articles.body:
Initial depth chart releases in the NFL are often unsurprising. Thanks to the lead-up from the summer, and some common sense, we usually have a pretty good idea of how teams will stack up going into the start of the regular season.

The Carolina Panthers revealed their first depth chart of the 2026 campaign on Tuesday. And although largely expected, the ranks did include a few intriguing placements.

Here are our biggest takeaways from the Panthers' first unofficial depth chart ahead of their Week 1 matchup against the Chicago Bears :

As anticipated, Tommy Tremble is listed as Carolina's starting tight end with 2025 fifth-round pick Mitchell Evans backing him up at No. 2. But the room gets a little interesting after that.

Former Pro Bowler Darren Waller , who was signed three weeks ago, has jumped 2024 fourth-rounder Ja'Tavion Sanders for the No. 3 spot. Waller just received high praise from head coach Dave Canales, who told reporters on Monday that the soon-to-be 34-year-old is looking " big and fast " in practice.

His placement could be an indication that the coaching staff is comfortable in keeping him active for Sunday, as well as an indictment on Sanders' outlook. The Panthers had hoped that Sanders would provide some much-needed receiving production at the tight end position, but have seen him amass just 532 yards and two touchdowns over his two seasons.

Waller seems to be angling for that role, as Sanders—who has been the subject of some recent trade rumors —continues to be phased out.

Meanwhile, special teams ace Feleipe Franks , who did impress as a pass catcher during the preseason, rounds out the bunch at No. 5.

In what may be a mild surprise to some, 2026 second-round pick Lee Hunter has overtaken second-year lineman Cam Jackson for a starting spot in the defensive trench. Instead of waiting for the 6-foot-3, 318-pound rookie to keep working his way up the totem pole, Carolina has decided that he's already primed for the responsibility.

Perhaps Hunter's presence can help ease the burden on his fellow starters, the Browns —Derrick and Bobby. The former could use a bit of help eating up blockers while the latter is trying to bounce back from a disappointing start to his three-year, $21 million pact.

Hunter, who tallied 2.5 sacks and a total of 10.5 tackles for a loss at Texas Tech in 2025, might be able to provide the push this unit needed last season.

With running back and primary returner Trevor Etienne on injured reserve, wideout Jimmy Horn Jr. has been noted as the leading man for both kick and punt duties.

A fan favorite for his speed, grit and clutch factor, Horn finally has the opening to make a difference on a more consistent basis. He has looked rather comfortable in his chances as a returner, and his quickness and suddenness could help bring Carolina's special teams to another level.

Although Etienne served relatively well in this job as a rookie, he doesn't match the excitement and home-run ability Horn brings to the field.

Horn is backed by fellow receiver Xavier Legette and starting running back Chuba Hubbard .

articles.title: Pocono Mountain West's Week 2 contest stretched over two days due to lightning
articles.summary: Football is tough, but having one game stretch over two days? That was a challenge Pocono Mountain West or Lehighton didn't see coming.
articles.body:
Pocono Mountain West football fell to Lehighton in Week 2 | Photos

POCONO SUMMIT — A football game, although varying in length, is usually completed in one calendar day. However, there are times where one game, like the Week 2 meeting between Pocono Mountain West and Lehighton, turns into a multi-day affair.

The Panthers' 35-0 loss to Lehighton started Thursday evening at 7 p.m. West quickly found itself in a 14-0 hole at the end of the first quarter, which ended on a West fumble and one Lehighton play in the red zone. Early in the second quarter, Lehighton tacked on another score to make it 21-0.

It appeared the game was going to end rather early on Thursday, until the lightning that lit up the sky moved close enough to the school where it couldn't be ignored anymore. The game was put on pause, and while some fans elected to leave soon after the delay, others tried waiting it out. But that became futile as the lightning flashes continued.

Soon, the game was called for the day, and the West athletic administration tried their best to pin down a continuation date as soon as possible. Luckily, officials and a doctor were available on Friday, and with the Pocono Mountain school district closed on Friday for Labor Day Weekend, the game was scheduled to resume the next day...

That was the only choice since the Friday evening slate was packed and Saturday wouldn't have been ideal either. So, at a time where most people on a holiday weekend would ease into the morning, the Pocono Mountain West and Lehighton coaches, players, and fans (though not as many as Thursday) made their way into the stadium for the second act.

West head coach Jim McCarroll was optimistic about the restart, saying, "I mean, it's tough, but I told them, 'Hey, new day, fresh start. Let's go out and just get better.' We're down 21-0. I didn't care. I said it's another opportunity to get better. You don't get the day back. Let's see where we're at."

The Panthers did come out with some renewed energy. but after Lehighton scored at the halftime buzzer, the spark all but dissipated. The final nail in the coffin was West threatening to score in the fourth quarter after the Stiehler brothers – Teddy with a big catch and Christian with a big run – got the Panthers into scoring position. But that momentum was short-lived as the drive ended with an interception in the end zone.

It was the polar opposite outcome of Pocono Mountain West's Week 1 showcase against Scranton, but McCarroll believes there are more positives to come from his team as the season progresses.

"I believe in them. They guys got to work and believe in themselves," McCarroll said. "Keep working hard. Not point fingers. 'Pull the thumb' as we always talk about."

West ends its nonconference slate at home vs. Hazleton, then starts EPC play at home vs. Dieruff before hitting the road vs. East Stroudsburg North.

articles.title: Andy Reid on practice goals for Patrick Mahomes to start in Week 1
articles.summary: During Tuesday's press conference, Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid revealed practice goals for Patrick Mahomes to start Week 1 | @EdEastonJr
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs begin the 2026 regular season next Monday night, hosting the Denver Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium for Week 1. Head coach Andy Reid, speaking with reporters Tuesday, revealed an important update on quarterback Patrick Mahomes ' playing status.

"Patrick (Mahomes) will go ahead and start unless something were to come up here in the next couple (of) days," said Reid. "But most likely, he'll be the guy that's out there."

Reid further detailed what he'd like to see this week to feel comfortable starting in Week 1 against the Broncos.

"Yeah, I mean, (Patrick Mahomes) he's shown everything there, "said Reid. "He hasn't missed a day, as you know, and you guys have seen him out there, so you know what it looks like- him running around and doing his stuff. Other than having a brace on his leg, everything looks normal. He's running around the same way he's always done and throwing the ball like he's always done. So, I think we're fine there."

Mahomes didn't play in the preseason but was active warming up before games while fully or a ting with the team. He is under a year removed from suffering the devastating knee injury in Week 15 last season.

articles.title: Patriots rule TreVeyon Henderson out for Wednesday night
articles.summary: Running back TreVeyon Henderson will not be in the lineup for the Patriots in Seattle on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
Running back TreVeyon Henderson will not be in the lineup for the Patriots in Seattle on Wednesday night.

Henderson has missed the last two weeks of practice with an ankle injury, so it came as no surprise that the Patriots officially ruled him out for their season opener on Tuesday. The Patriots previously announced that offensive lineman Ben Brown will miss the game with a knee injury and no other players have injury designations.

Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner are the other running backs on the 53-man roster for New England . Hassan Haskins and Lan Larison are available to be elevated from the practice squad.

The Patriots will also be summoning punter Mitch Wishnowsky from the practice squad as they are currently without a punter on their active roster.

articles.title: Is TreVeyon Henderson playing Week 1? Latest injury update for Patriots RB
articles.summary: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson is preparing for his second NFL season. Will he play in Week 1 against the Seahawks as he battles an ankle injury?
articles.body:
The New England Patriots are going to be down one of their key offensive playmakers as they open the 2026 NFL season against the Seattle Seahawks .

Running back TreVeyon Henderson will not play in the Wednesday, Sept. 9, season opener as he deals with an ankle injury.

Henderson originally suffered the ankle injury in practice on Aug. 24 after slipping during a drill. He hasn't returned to the field since and was listed as a non-participant at each of New England 's final three practices ahead of their matchup against Seattle.

Henderson was expected to be a key part of New England's one-two punch at running back alongside Rhamondre Stevenson . The 23-year-old back generated 1,132 scrimmage yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie while handling 215 touches. He finished third in the NFL's Offensive Rookie of the Year Award voting because of his strong performance.

Here's more to know about Henderson's injury and when Patriots fans and fantasy football managers may see him return to the field.

See which of the eight new 'Rivalries' NFL uniforms make a statement

Henderson will not play for the Patriots in their Week 1 game against the Seahawks. He was ruled out on the team's final injury report, which was released on Tuesday, Sept. 8.

Henderson did not practice in the lead-up to the Patriots vs. Seahawks matchup and was listed as a non-participant at each of the team's three sessions from Monday to Wednesday.

Henderson is dealing with an ankle injury that he suffered in practice on Aug. 24. He missed New England's final preseason game against the Cleveland Browns and his status for Week 1 was viewed as uncertain.

Henderson has yet to practice since the initial injury occurred. Patriots coach Mike Vrabel praised Henderson's recovery efforts in a recent news conference but did not provide a concrete update on whether he would play in Week 1.

"We'll see how he feels today. We'll see if he can do anything," Vrabel said on Monday, Sept. 7 , when referencing the second-year running back. "He's been working extremely hard to come back, and we'll see where that goes here today. We do have a few more days before, but we'll see what he's able to do today."

Vrabel did not hold a news conference Tuesday and, thus, did not provide any additional update on Henderson's status.

The Patriots have not provided a concrete update about Henderson's potential return to the lineup. The Patriots play the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 2 on Sunday, Sept. 20, giving the Ohio State product 11 extra days to recover for that contest.

Henderson is technically listed as the No. 2 running back on the Patriots' depth chart behind Stevenson. That makes the team's third-string running back, Corey Kiner , Henderson's backup.

That said, Stevenson would be expected to handle a lion's share of the work with Henderson out of the lineup. Kiner was only acquired from the Arizona Cardinals in a trade on Aug. 29, so he has only had a couple of weeks to ingratiate himself into Josh McDaniels' offense.

The Patriots have three running backs on their 53-man roster to open the season. Below is a look at the pecking order within the unit:

The Patriots also have second-year back Lan Larison and veteran Hassan Haskins on the practice squad. One is expected to be called up for Wednesday's game with Henderson out of action and Kiner being new to the team.

Larison, a second-year player who went undrafted out of UC Davis, would likely get the nod if the Patriots value experience in their offensive system for the potential backup role behind Stevenson.

Haskins, who was originally drafted by the Tennessee Titans when Vrabel was there and has played 44 NFL games and logged 76 carries, would get the call-up if the Patriots want to emphasize overall experience behind Stevenson.

Pittsburgh Steelers rookie Max Iheanachor's home was recently burglarized, a spokesperson for the team confirmed to Channel 11.

According to a Pittsburgh Public Safety spokesperson, the burglary happened on Bradley Street in Duquesne Heights between 10:30 a.m. and 1:30 p.m. on Aug. 26.

No one was home when the burglary happened.

Initial reports said the caller noticed a garage door that had been closed was now open and a window was broken by a rock.

About $157,000 worth of jewelry, Rolex watches and designer bags were reported missing.

Iheanachor was the Steelers' first-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.

He recently returned to the field after recovering from an apparent neck and shoulder injury.

articles.title: Porto vs. Man City score, stats, highlights as Haaland double seals points for Maresca's men
articles.summary: Erling Haaland was the difference once again as Manchester City got their Champions League campaign underway with a 2-0 win at Porto.
articles.body:
Erling Haaland was the difference once again as Manchester City got their Champions League campaign underway with a 2-0 win at Porto.

The Norway superstar scored the only goal as City beat Coventry 1-0 at the weekend and his second-half brace saw off Francesco Farioli's side in a hard-fought affair at Estadio do Dragao.

Haaland's game-sealing second, when he slotted home substitute Rayan Ait-Nouri's pass in the first minute of stoppage time, was his 36th in the Champions League for City, to equal Sergio Aguero 's club record. He also moved up to third on Manchester City 's all-time scoring charts with 167.

City were patient in the face of Porto's aggressive press and gradually took control of the opening half.

Porto were indebted to Diogo Costa for keeping the deadlock intact at the break with two stunning pieces of goalkeeping. First, the Portugal international produced a point-blank stop to deny Haaland from close range on the end of Antoine Semenyo 's cross, before thwarting Haaland and Rayan Cherki with a double reaction stop.

But keeping Haaland at bay for a prolonged period remains one of the toughest tasks in soccer and, when Enzo Fernandez found him with a dinked cross within two minutes of the restart, he nodded in his fourth of the season via the post

After taking the lead, City's poise deserved them. Alan Varella drove inches wide of the post right, and Gianluigi Donnarumma was relieved to see the ball skid wide of the other upright when he drilled a clearance into the onrushing William Gomes .

Porto have won five out of five domestically this term, but as they strained to avert a first home loss since December, chances started to present themselves at the other end. Haaland never needs too many invitations.

Location: Estadio do Dragao (Porto, Portugal) Referee: Szymon Marciniak (Poland)

Porto (4-3-3, right to left): 99. Diogo Costa (GK) — 20. Alberto Costa, 18. Nehuen Perez, 4. Jakub Kiwior , 52. Martim Fernandes —13. Pablo Rosario , 22. Alan Varela , 10. Gabri Veiga — 7. William Gomes, 19. Andre Silva, 11. Pepe

Man City (4-2-3-1, right to left): 1. Gianluigi Donnarumma (GK) — 27. Matheus Nunes , 3. Ruben Dias , 6. Marc Guehi , 24. Josko Gvardiol — 17, Enzo Fernandez, 32. Ayyoub Bouaddi — 47. Phil Foden , 10. Rayan Cherki, 42. Antoine Semenyo — 9. Erling Haaland

Porto vs. Man City highlights, key incidents

Porto have pushed hard for the equaliser but left an increasing number of spaces at the back. Rayan Ait-Nouri finds one of those and the City substitute tees up Haaland to slot home a low finish. Next!

City couldn't make their pressure count in the first half but they're in front now. Foden and Semenyo are involved as Cherki tries to go around Diogo Costa. He can't, but manages to keep the attack alive, Fernandez dinks a cross towards Haaland and the big man finds an uncharacteristically deft header that nestles in the net via the post.

Superb once again by Porto's goalkeeper. City engineer some room down the right channel and Foden crosses for Haaland, who hammers it back the way it came on the volley. It looks destined for the bottom corner but Diogo Costa reacts superbly and it then comes out to sprawl in the way of Cherki's follow-up. A heavy touch from Semenyo on the next rebound means the chance is gone.

21' Brilliant save from Diogo Costa to deny Haaland

City have hogged the ball calmly without creating too much but Foden and Semenyo quicken the tempo nicely. The latter hangs up a cross for Haaland to meet at the back post. Diogo Costa has minimal time to react but claws it away brilliantly.

articles.title: Newcastle edge past Millwall to progress in Carabao Cup
articles.summary: Newcastle edged past Championship side Millwall with a 1-0 win in the third round of the EFL Cup.Joe Willock’s late goal separated the sides, but Newcastle c...
articles.body:
Newcastle edged past Championship side Millwall with a 1-0 win in the third round of the EFL Cup .

Joe Willock 's late goal separated the sides, but Newcastle could have been behind moments earlier when Tairyk Arconte smashed an effort against the post.

Despite the late scare, Newcastle controlled the match and could have had more as Fabian Schar , Yoane Wissa and Harvey Barnes all missed big chances to make the result more comfortable.

Over the last three years, Newcastle have made the EFL Cup their favourite competition. Either side of winning it in 2025, they reached the semi-finals and the quarter-final stage.

Despite all the changes in the club over the summer, Newcastle, now led by Matthias Jaissle, have not changed their attitude to this tournament.

Willock created the first meaningful chance of the evening. The Englishman drove into the box on the left-hand side before firing a powerful effort on goal. Filip Marschall did well to save, but the Newcastle onslaught did not stop there.

Minutes later Schar's free header looped just over the bar from a corner, before Barnes tried his luck from range with a similar result.

Even though Newcastle were on top, Millwall did have chances. Midway through the first half, the Premier League side's defence was almost breached when Lyndon Dykes got on the end of a searching cross into the box. His inventive effort was comfortably saved, however.

Newcastle remained on top for the rest of the first half, but still failed to find the back of the net. Ramsey and Wissa both had good chances to at least test Marschall in the Millwall goal, but both efforts were wide of the mark.

After the break, Millwall looked like a completely changed outfit. Minutes after the restart, Jenson Metcalfe fired an effort over the bar and Millwall's chances did not end there.

Caleb Taylor's uncontested header five minutes later from a wide free kick sailed just wide of the post, but despite facing 14 shots from a strong Newcastle side in the first half, the south London team were showing they weren't just here to take part.

The response did not last long though, as Jaissle played his hand. Anthony Elanga and summer signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo were both introduced and a similar pattern resumed.

With ten minutes to go and penalties looming, Newcastle did have their breakthrough. Minutes after Arconte saw Millwall's golden chance to take the lead rattle the post, Willock scored the goal that looked like it had been coming all game.

Excellent play from Fernandez-Pardo and Lewis Hall on the left created space for the left back, who fired in a low cross for his compatriot to pass the ball home.

articles.title: Falcons reveal two rookies starting on defense Week 1 vs. Steelers
articles.summary: Atlanta to start a rookie linebacker and rookie nickel vs. Pittsburgh
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons have released their first official depth chart of the 2026 NFL season ahead of Sunday's opener on the road against the Pittsburgh Steelers .

There's not much in the way of surprises after three preseason games and 37 cuts last weekend to bring the roster down to 53 for the regular season. There are a few interesting notes, though, including two of the team's 2026 draft picks being listed in the starting lineup for Week 1.

The first of them will be lining up next to Divine Deablo at the second level at off-ball linebacker. That's where rookie Kendal Daniels has beaten out veteran Christian Harris for the right to start.

Daniels spent four years at Oklahoma State before transferring to Oklahoma for his final college season. All together he appeared in 54 games at the college level , totaling 293 tackles, five interceptions, 16 passes defensed and 7.5 sacks. A fourth-round pick by Atlanta, Daniels impressed during the preseason with his size and physical style that may remind some fans of former Falcons linebacker De'Vondre Campbell.

The first challenge for Daniels will be helping to slow down the Steelers' run game, led by Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle . Expect Daniels to also be challenged in coverage by tight ends Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington .

On the back end of Jeff Ulbrich's defense there's another rookie to be found in the form of the Falcons' second-round pick, former Clemson cornerback Avieon Terrell - the younger brother of A.J. Terrell. In 39 college games , Terrell totaled three interceptions, 25 passes defensed, nine tackles for a loss and eight forced fumbles.

Atlanta plans to play the younger Terrell both in the slot and on the boundary, but to begin his career he'll be starting at the nickel spot that fell to Billy Bowman Jr . last season.

Bowman is still not 100 percent, so we'll see if he returns to the starting lineup once healthy. In the meantime, Terrell's main selling points are his ball skills and a tenacious style for a defender his size.

The rookie's first matchup in the slot will come against Steelers receiver Roman Wilson . You won't find any rookies in the starting lineup on the other side of the ball. The closest thing is Zachariah Branch, who's listed as second in the slot behind returning veteran Olamide Zaccheaus .

articles.summary: Braves starting pitcher Bryce Elder underwent surgery on his right knee Tuesday and will be out three to four weeks, manager Walt Weiss said.  Weiss said the...
articles.body:
ATLANTA (AP) — Braves starting pitcher Bryce Elder underwent surgery on his right knee Tuesday and will be out three to four weeks, manager Walt Weiss said.

Weiss said the right-hander, who has made 26 starts this season, has been dealing with discomfort in his knee since the All-Star break, and it got to the point where he needed to have the procedure done if he hoped to be able to pitch in the postseason. Elder flew from Philadelphia to Dallas, where he had the surgery.

Elder is 8-8 with a 4.11 ERA this season. He is second on the Braves behind Chris Sale with 15 quality starts.

"In the first half, he was one of the best pitchers on our staff," Weiss said. "He tried to fight through it. He got to a point where we couldn't really do it anymore."

Weiss said Reynaldo López will replace Elder in the Braves' six-man rotation moving forward and likely will start Wednesday.

López has made 11 starts this season but has been on the injured list with left knee inflammation for six weeks. He made three rehab starts with Triple-A Gwinnett. López is 4-3 with a 3.64 ERA in 24 appearances.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 1 Panic Meter: Young RBs highlight players we're worried about to start 2026
articles.summary: Ray Garvin takes you through his panic meter heading into Week 1 fantasy football in 2026.
articles.body:
It is Week 1, and the last thing I want to do is incite panic among a group of fantasy football managers who have been waiting all offseason for this moment. We drafted these teams, talked ourselves into these players and have been waiting for real football to finally get here. The last thing you want to hear before setting your first lineup is somebody telling you to worry about one of the players you drafted.

But think about it this way. There are some legitimate concerns heading into Week 1, and I would much rather know about those concerns now and set my expectations accordingly than find out when the games start. So these are panics, but they are loose panics. We are not burying anybody before the season starts. This is simply about identifying where there may be a little more risk than we anticipated when we drafted these players.

Let's start with Dak Prescott because this one caught my attention immediately. Tyler Smith is going to have surgery on his thumb and is expected to miss 4-6 weeks. Smith is one of the best guards in football, and Dallas is going to open the season against the Giants, Commanders, Ravens and Texans without arguably the best player on its offensive line.

Then, you look at the rest of that offensive line and there are reasons to be concerned. Terence Steele allowed 52 pressures last season, which is not good, and now T.J. Bass is being asked to step into Smith's spot. Dallas has some difficult defensive fronts coming up early, so I understand why people may look at this situation and wonder whether Dak should be downgraded.

I am not there yet. Dak still has CeeDee Lamb , George Pickens and Jake Ferguson . This is still an offense we expect to throw the football a lot, and Dak is still a veteran quarterback who has shown he can operate at a high level when things are not perfect around him.

Would I rather have Smith protecting him? Of course. Does losing Smith make these first few games more difficult? Absolutely. But if Prescott is the quarterback you drafted to start for your fantasy team, I am not changing that because of this injury.

This one is different because my concern with Ashton Jeanty is mainly about what we do not know. The Raiders have been pretty vague about exactly what this ankle injury is and, more importantly, what it could mean for Jeanty's workload in Week 1.

That is what I want to know. Is he good to go? And I do not mean, "Is he active?" I mean, is Jeanty actually ready to play a normal workload? Because those are two completely different questions.

How many times have we seen a player get cleared, everybody gets excited because he is active and then the game starts and he is standing on the sideline for half the snaps? That is what worries me here.

Mike Washington Jr. complicates this because Washington has done enough throughout the summer to give the Raiders confidence in him. I am not saying Washington is taking Jeanty's job. That is not what this is about. But if Jeanty is only 80-85%, does Las Vegas really have to push him for 20-plus touches in Week 1? Probably not.

If Jeanty is active, you are probably going to play him. He is just one of those players. I get it. But we need to prepare ourselves for the possibility that "active" does not mean "full workload."

There is definitely some panic around Malik Nabers, and I understand it. He is coming back from the ACL injury, he did not do a ton of back-to-back work throughout training camp and now you are asking him to step into Week 1 in a brand new offense.

There are already people in fantasy who are a little apprehensive about this Matt Nagy-led offense. Now Nabers has to find his rhythm with Jaxson Dart and, more importantly than anything else, trust his knee again when the game starts moving at full speed.

You can be medically cleared, you can practice and you can run routes. At some point, though, Nabers has to plant that foot, make a hard cut with somebody closing on him and not think about the knee.

The good news is the Giants certainly seem to have confidence in where he is. They released Darius Slayton and are heading into the season with Nabers, Darnell Mooney , Malachi Fields and Odell Beckham Jr. at wide receiver. Whatever we may think about Nabers' Week 1 workload, New York has to feel pretty good about his timeline if that is the wide receiver room it is comfortable taking into the season.

And Nabers is still Nabers. We already know what this player can do when the football is coming his way. My concern is simply whether we see the full Malik Nabers immediately. That is enough for some panic, but it is nowhere near enough panic for me to stay away from him if he is playing.

Jeremiyah Love is in a very similar spot to Jeanty for me. You are talking about a rookie running back, the third overall pick in the NFL Draft and a player who already showed us in the preseason why Arizona was so excited about him.

We know he can play. That is not the question. The question is why Arizona would rush him back if it does not have to. Love is coming off a high-ankle sprain, and we have to remember the difference between being able to play and being ready for the workload fantasy managers want.

If Love is active in Week 1, you are going to consider starting him. I understand that. But Arizona brought in Tyler Allgeier for exactly this type of situation. This is a former 1,000-yard rusher and a veteran running back who has already handled NFL carries. If Arizona needs somebody to take 15 touches for a week or two while Love gets completely healthy, I think it feels pretty comfortable asking Allgeier to do that.

So if Love is technically available but Arizona thinks another week of managing his workload will help him get right, why would it push him? This is Week 1 of a very long season.

Long term, I am not worried about Jeremiyah Love. Week 1 is different. If I have another good option, I would rather not play him until I actually see what this workload looks like.

Now, we get to the one that actually concerns me. TreVeyon Henderson is total panic. I do not want to put him in the "Coping Corner" yet because we are not there, but this is problematic.

The reason this is different from Jeanty and Love is that Henderson's issue did not just pop up a couple of days before Week 1. We have been hearing about this for a while now. He has been dealing with the ankle injury that has held him out of practice for weeks and the Patriots ruled Henderson out for the opener Wednesday vs. the Seahawks .

My concern isn't just Henderson missing Week 1. It is what happens after Week 1, because while Henderson has been unavailable, everything we have heard about Rhamondre Stevenson has been positive. Stevenson has looked good, operated as the RB1 and been the guy New England trusts in this backfield.

That was already part of the concern with Henderson before the injury. We drafted Henderson because we believe in the talent, and I believe in the talent. But talent was never the problem. The question was whether Henderson could take enough of this backfield away from Stevenson to become the fantasy option we wanted him to be.

Now, Henderson is hurt, which makes that path even more difficult. And let me be clear: this is not about dropping TreVeyon Henderson. Absolutely not, not even close. He is way too talented, and things can change very quickly at running back.

But starting him when healthy is a different conversation. I cannot do that right now. Even when he gets cleared, I would need to see what this role actually looks like before feeling comfortable putting him into my lineup.

Henderson has an injury layered on top of a role that was already more questionable than fantasy managers wanted it to be. That is why this one is different.

We are not in "Coping Corner" yet, but we are absolutely already in "Total Panic."

articles.title: MAC files appeal to FBS committee to overturn Western Michigan-Michigan game, declare Broncos as winners
articles.summary: The MAC filed a formal NCAA appeal claiming the Western Michigan Broncos should be recognized as winners after a replay protocol error at Michigan.
articles.body: For a few minutes, the most stunning result of the early part of the college football season seemed to be the Western Michigan Broncos upsetting the heavily favored Michigan Wolverines at Michigan Stadium. The Big House. Bryce Underwood, one of the most heavily promoted recruits of the past decade. New head coach Kyle Whittingham, known for his stability, consistency and avoiding major upsets while with the Utah Utes. And the Broncos took a 12-7 lead with just 38 seconds remaining and the Wolverines out of timeouts. Everyone knows what happened next. Underwood's first Hail Mary attempt flew out of the back of the endzone, with the game clock on the broadcast and scoreboard showing 0:00. Game over. But after a poorly-explained review determined that there should have been an additional second added, Underwood was given a second opportunity. JJ Buchanan came down with it, and Wolverines fans stormed the field. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSIBLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Nearly everyone outside Michigan was perplexed, or downright angry, about the outcome. The Big Ten's explanation didn't make anything better either, with the conference saying the clocks were strobe-synced prior to the game, but that another clock viewed during the replay process had determined there was a second left. Even though the synced cameras showed zero seconds remaining. Initially, it seemed like that would be the end of it. Western Michigan staff said they communicated with the Big Ten, reviewed the footage and were satisfied that proper procedure had been followed. Tuesday afternoon, though, that all changed. The Mid-American Conference released a statement, announcing they'd filed a formal appeal to the NCAA FBS Oversight Committee and the College Football Playoff requesting that those two bodies recognize the Broncos as the true winners of the game. "After further study and investigation, it is now evident that replay protocol was not properly followed in determining whether time remained on the game clock at the conclusion of the Western Michigan vs. Michigan football game," the statement says. "The established replay protocol requires that the game clock displayed on the program feed be used in determining whether time remained. Instead, the Big Ten Conference replay crew relied upon the clock feed embedded within its replay system. As a result, one second was placed back on the game clock and an additional play was awarded." CRAIG CARTON BLASTS MICHIGAN FANS FOR STORMING FIELD AFTER CONTROVERSIAL WIN: 'THEY’RE A BUNCH OF MORONS' Interestingly, they also stress that the appeal isn't contesting the correct amount of time on the clock, just that the rules were improperly applied. "This was not a judgment regarding the proper amount of time to place on the clock," it continues. "It was an error in the application of the established replay protocol governing this specific end-of-game timing situation. Had the protocol been properly followed and the program-feed clock been used, no additional play would have been awarded, and Western Michigan would have won the game, 12–7." MICHIGAN FANS CALLED OUT ON SOCIAL MEDIA FOR RUSHING FIELD AFTER WOLVERINES STEAL WIN OVER WESTERN MICHIGAN The conference, as a result, want the NCAA FBS Oversight Committee and College Football to recognize the Western Michigan Broncos as the "actual winner." "The MAC is requesting that those bodies recognize Western Michigan as the actual winner of the game for purposes of their respective rankings, evaluations and selection deliberations, and take such other corrective action as may be within their authority," the statement concludes. So what does the NCAA rule book actually say about this procedure, and does the MAC have a point? The closest relevant rule seems to govern what video evidence can be evaluated as part of a review. And while it's not overwhelmingly clear what the proper procedure should be, there is an indication that the "televised production" should be used when evaluating video evidence. OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD "All reviews shall be based upon video evidence provided by and coming directly from the televised production of the game or from other video means available to the replay official that is also available to the television producer," the rule says. So what chance does the MAC have at getting the result overturned? Very little. Even if there is some truth to this appeal, and the result was unfair to Western Michigan, it's a near impossibility that an FBS Committee overturns a result that was determined on the field. And it goes without saying that big programs like Michigan are a near-certainty to get the benefit of the doubt in these types of cases. But the MAC at least showed some backbone and support for its member school after that debacle and what it cost them. Western Michigan may have contended for a College Football Playoff spot, with the benefit of a win over a top-20 opponent, had the game ended at 0:00. In response, the Big Ten issued a statement of their own, saying, "The Big Ten stands by the statement released following the conclusion of the Western Michigan at Michigan game and the determination by the replay officials. We will have no further comment on the matter." Sums up where both sides are, and why this controversy will never reach a satisfactory resolution for all involved parties.

articles.title: Ex-NFL star Shawne Merriman gives take on pro players trying to return to college: 'Pretty ridiculous'
articles.summary: Shawne Merriman called Lane Kiffin's LSU Tigers eligibility controversy "ridiculous" and warns without guardrails, former pros returning won't stop.
articles.body: College football may be fully underway, but a dark cloud hovers over the landscape amid the controversy involving players who got professional experience trying to get back into the ranks with some of the best programs in the country, namely Lane Kiffin’s LSU Tigers program. The latest from the SEC was an amended complaint filed on Tuesday morning in an Alabama federal court, which indicated the conference wishes to take some serious action against LSU after commissioner Greg Sankey stood in a Baton Rouge courtroom last week to argue the school, Lane Kiffin and the athletic department staffers were preventing the use of First Amendment rights to govern the conference. All of this to say college athletics has reached a point where former NFL and Maryland Terrapins linebacker Shawne Merriman can’t believe his eyes. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM "I think it’s pretty ridiculous," he told OutKick about athletes returning to college to get their fifth year of eligibility despite going pro just months ago. "Look, I’ve met Lane Kiffin plenty of times. I think he’s great. I got no problem for him wanting to win by putting whoever he can on the roster and making the situation better. "But there have to be guardrails, because it won’t stop here if you don’t stop it now. That’s the issue." Merriman added that college athletics has "always been pure," and even with name, image and likeness (NIL) deals becoming a key component of why these athletes are willing to stay, or even return, to Division I sports, he believes there was some decorum everyone could agree on. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Now, it’s a free-for-all, with athletes jumping through the transfer portal chasing the next biggest check from colleges and universities to play for them. And with the NCAA ruling that college athletes have five years to use five seasons of eligibility, players like tight end Dae’Quan Wright, who played four years of college football before going undrafted and getting cut by the Cleveland Browns, are trying to return to play their fifth year in college. "There has to be some guardrails with the transferring," Merriman added. "Guys being able to take NIL money, then getting up to leave and go to another program. Now, it’s just kind of the tipping point where a former professional athlete can go back into college. It’s just too much. If they don’t stop it now, it’s never going to stop." Amid the college debacle, the NFL sent a memo to its clubs reminding them that players who return to college to play wouldn’t be eligible to be signed during the season. Furthermore, those players are no longer eligible for an NFL Draft, meaning they would have to join an NFL team at some point in a future season as a free agent. But if that player does end up in a locker room, how would the rest of the team react knowing what happened? Will there be some distain from teammates? "I think it’s going to be a silent yes," Merriman responded when posed the same question. "I don’t think a lot of guys will be vocal to it. I even think the NFL is going to have a silence behind it but have a problem with it. There’s been plenty of guys through the past few decades or so that just didn’t cut it, right? For whatever reason, they didn’t make the roster. Maybe they got injured, maybe the coaching staff saw they didn’t line up with their scheme. Plenty of reasons, so why do you get an opportunity to go back and do something else and return? "Look, I don’t think the return will be taken the right way trying to get back into an NFL locker room because, at that point, all kinds of things will be questioned -- Integrity, motive, what kind of guy this is. I’m not going to say that will be the pinpoint conversations, but I think there will be a lot of silence behind closed doors with people having a problem with it." What plays out in the courtroom remains to be seen, but as a team like LSU continues its pursuit of a national championship, Merriman knows this controversy can pose a threat to focus. COLTS GM CHRIS BALLARD RIPS NFL PLAYERS RETURNING TO COLLEGE FOOTBALL: 'STUPIDEST S--- I’VE EVER HEARD' "It’s a distraction. There’s a high-risk, low reward to get a couple of guys go out and go play," he said. "What about the rest of the team that’s got to answer questions? Instead of talking about the game, they’re talking about this. So, I just think that the risk is just too high, and the reward is too low to fight this battle, especially now with the SEC and committee stepping in as a whole." Merriman is also focused on the college landscape considering his son, Justin Merriman, is on a path to Division I football in his own right. Justin is one of the top quarterback prospects for the 2029 class, a 6-foot-3-and-a-half quarterback for St. Frances Academy (Baltimore, Maryland), the no. 2-ranked high school program in the country by MaxPreps. The elder Merriman said he’s grateful to watch his son at this stage of his football career, where he can offer guidance and direction in a world completely different from when he was on his way to playing for Maryland before becoming a first-round NFL Draft pick by the San Diego Chargers. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "He makes all his own decisions, but to be that resource for him and let him know some of this guidance and which directions to take has been really cool for me," Merriman said. Justin and St. Frances Academy will be taking on IMG Academy later this season, and it’s not just a clash between two of the top teams in the country, but the latest chapter of a bitter rivalry for these two programs. They kick off on Nov. 13 at St. Frances, which Merriman said is likely to be the most-watched high school football game in the country this season.

He did return to practice Sunday and also practiced Monday, and coach Sean McVay said Garrett will play in the season opener against the Rams on Thursday.

Garrett didn't answer how he felt physically, stating simply that he's ready for the season opener despite the lack of training camp reps.

"I think I'll be able to play off of some great teammates," Garrett said, via Benjamin Royer of ocregister.com. "We have a strong defense all around, and they'll make it easy, even if I am a touch off of what I usually am. I don't suspect that I will be, but I have plenty of support , that's all I'm saying."

Garrett set the NFL record with 23 sacks last season, winning his second Defensive Player of the Year award. But late last season, that's all he and the Browns had to play for.

It was that way for most of his career in Cleveland , with the Browns going 58-90 with two playoff appearances in Garrett's nine seasons there. The Rams' aspirations are much higher.

"Super Bowl," Garrett said. "Win DPOY again, obviously. I think those are the two main things on my mind, and going out and just being the best player I can be. I think there is a whole bunch of opportunities out there for, for us as the D-line to be something truly special, and I just want us to be able to realize that and, and never go into the locker room after a game feeling like we could've achieved more or done more."

articles.title: Brad White says Florida's defense must find its killer instinct
articles.summary: Brad White broke down Florida's defensive shortcomings against FAU, the need for greater awareness and what must improve before Campbell.
articles.body:
Allowing 21 points to Florida Atlantic left Brad White with a "pit in his stomach" after Florida 's defense failed to meet his standard in Week 1.

The Gators ' defensive coordinator credited the unit for forcing three turnovers and making several critical stops, but he didn't dance around the problems handling tempo, recognizing situations and maintaining proper pass-rush technique.

White also discussed DJ Coleman 's immediate emergence as a leader, Brendan Bett 's development, Alfonzo Allen Jr.'s versatility and the lessons Florida must carry into its Week 2 matchup against Campbell.

PHOTOS: Highlights from Florida's season-opening win vs FAU Owls

What was your assessment of Florida's defensive performance against FAU?

I think we all see it the same way. In every game, there's going to be good, and there's bad. In the moment, immediately after the game, you've got that pit in your stomach because you know we could have played way better.

That was not the standard or the bar that we want to set for how to play defense around here. Again, a lot of it, when you watch the tape, wasn't an effort thing. It was an awareness thing, understanding football and basic football IQ.

The No. 1 goal we talked about was embracing the tempo. We knew it was going to be high-paced. We knew it was going to be different than expected. I think for a significant portion of the game, we did not do a good enough job. We let it get to us and dictate how we played.

There was a little bit of survival mode. We talked about what you can't do against that is get into that mode where, "I've just got to survive this down. I've got to survive." You've got to have a killer instinct and empty it on every play.

It's a really good learning experience. Are you happy with it? No. We're really glad that we won the game. Obviously, the offense played really, really well and relieved some of that pressure for those guys on defense.

But we need to take a significant step forward in terms of our mentality, how we play and our awareness on the football field. When you play with football awareness and football IQ, you see the good things that happen.

You see DJ Coleman's pick. They're in condensed spacing. You've repped it. We've seen it. We repped it against that play call, and he knew it. He saw it, jumped it and, boom, DJ did a nice job on the tip.

There were good things, but Coach always talks about that word "strain" and what that means. We need to learn how to say, "Hey, listen, there's that effort where you feel like you're giving everything, but when you don't think you can go any further, push even more."

When you say, "My car is straining," like when your car is straining up a hill, what does that mean? It is pushing beyond its limit. It's not just working hard to get up. There are cars that work, but if it's straining to get up, you can tell by the sound and by the look.

That's what we need from some of our guys.

What were the positives from the season opener?

The takeaways were good. On first and second down, did they get some first downs? Yeah. But that was the first time I've ever been part of 22 third downs. Then you tack on another seven fourth downs. There were 29 times when it was third or fourth down, and a lot of those were short to medium.

Hats off to them. They were a team sort of built on explosives, and they said, "You know what? We're going to just try to methodically do this thing."

When a team does that, our guys have to be able to adjust. When we come to the sideline and make an adjustment — "Hey, we've got to jump down. We've got to get sticky. It's third-and-2. It's third-and-4. We've got to get the call and understand what the down and distance is. This is a time to challenge."

We have to learn from that. We'll get better from that. But by no means is everybody's head down and this thing is over. This is a building process. They've got to learn how I call a game. I've got to learn how they adjust on the sideline and how they take coaching. How literal are they sometimes when you talk and give coaching points? Can they read the tone, or is everything super literal? Every guy is a little bit different, and I'm still learning.

There are some calls in there that I would like back. There was a third down in the red zone when I was trying to take away one route, and then they ran the run play. By taking away the route, I took the safety out of the run fit, so he was going to be late.

I tried to muck it up, and we just missed the tackle inside. That's a call I'd love to have back, especially as much as they were starting to run the ball on third down. I should have just said, "Hey, we can play the route in a one-on-one situation without safety help." Those are things, again, for all of us. You've got to raise your hand and ask, "How do I get better from Week 1 to Week 2?"

How would you evaluate Florida's pass rush?

It never felt really clean. It didn't feel like we were getting a ton of clean wins. There were a couple of other times when we were at the top of the pocket where I think our top-of-the-pocket mechanics could be better — how we reach and how we strain at the top.

On the one third down when he scrambled down to the 1-yard line, we ended up jetting up the B gap with our three-technique, and he got really high. We needed that edge rusher to naturally turn it into a game. That three-technique also has to understand, "If I don't win the B-gap right now within three yards, I have to counter. I've got to push the play."

Some of the rush lanes got a little bit off. In the first game, all the technique went out the window a little bit — the things that they've been working on. They all came in Sunday and Monday with kind of long faces, like, "Man, Coach, all that bad technique showed up on film."

I was like, "Yeah, because you let the moment and the game get bigger than the training." But they've got to learn from that. This is why we say, "Do what we do."

We've talked in here about touching the stove. The reality is that most young men these days don't learn from other people touching the stove. You can tell them it's hot. They can watch their teammate touch it and say, "Man, that looked like it really hurt. Hey, let me just touch it to see if it really does or if you're joking with me."

The problem is that you've got 11 guys all trying to do that. It's like, "Guys, we've got to learn from that guy."

We're getting there. Do we need to get better? Yeah. But I'm never going to come up here — whether you like it or not — and say the sky is falling.

It's a game. We're going to pour into our guys, and we're going to be really demanding of them. They understand that. It was a really good Tuesday practice today in terms of what we're trying to demand of them and the growth that we expect from them and us as coaches.

But we're still going to enjoy it. We're going to enjoy it because that's how you have swagger. If it's a doldrum and you feel like you just have to beat them down to a pulp, then they're not going to play for you.

Were the defensive backs instructed to play off the receivers on third-and-short?

It goes down to feel. The best part about playing in The Swamp is being in The Swamp, and it's 90,000 people being loud on third down. At that point, you as a coach cannot communicate anymore. It goes back to having to be trained, and we have not done a good enough job of getting those guys to truly understand every down and every distance.

I have to not just get the call, but I have to know the situation. It's third-and-1 on the goal line. It's third-and-1 in a logo-zone shot area. It's third-and-1 backed up. What are their offensive tendencies in all of those moments?

It can't just be, "Man, I'm so tired. It's been eight plays. Please, just somebody make a play. I can't get beat deep, so I'm going to back up."

You've got to dig deep in those situations. But we have to continue to do a better job as coaches because, in practice, if you're out there and we tell you, "Get out and press," they hear you.

We can be yelling as loudly as we can on the sideline during a game, but they can't hear us. They have to be able to operate. The only player I can talk to is the inside linebacker.

How much has Brendan Bett grown, and what does he provide the defensive line?

He's on a defense that is young in areas. There are some older guys whom people lean into. It's him. It's the Bryce Thorntons. It's the Myles Grahams. It's the guys who have been around here for a while.

They've been in games and understand the environment, so guys can lean into them. He's that force. He's that guy whom I can talk to and say, "Hey, this is what we're trying to get done. Can you sort of help me along?" I lean into him.

But even he is still young in his football development. I think people forget how young we are from a pure snap perspective on defense. There's maturity that we have to go through, and there's a football maturity that we have to develop as a defense.

Even Bett, as a guy, understands that he's learning how to control the emotional aspect of football. He is emotional in a good way, but that still needs to be harnessed and controlled so he can play at his best and doesn't get down on himself if he's not making every play.

He wants to do right so badly. It's like, "Hey, man, it's not going to be perfect. But play with effort and play with strain."

Maybe my favorite play of the entire game was the fourth-down stop. Not for any reason other than it was the end of the game. Essentially, the game was in hand, but you want to talk about what strain looks like? That wasn't just effort. That was strain to finish the series and not let them in.

We came out of that timeout and said, "Guys, this is going to tell me something about our football character as a defense. Are we going to lay down? Are we just going to go through the motions and then sing the fight song afterward, or are you going to take this personally?"

When we say we defend every blade of grass, is that just words, or is that in action? You saw it from everybody, but you really saw it from No. 90 on that play.

What did you see in DJ Coleman before bringing him to Florida?

That's another one. You're talking about a senior guys trust and learn from. I referenced guys who have been here, but as quickly as DJ has been here, he has elevated himself into a leadership position on our team. So much of it is just through his work and how he goes about his business.

He's very much in that mold of being a pro's pro. He's here early and stays late. He's going to watch all the film. As much data as we can give him, he wants to take and absorb.

By no means was it perfect, but it was a really high-effort game. The interception and then the forced interception were really big plays. Obviously, you start the game with the pick. Then they had the two touchdown drives, and you're reeling a little bit. It was like, "OK, let's see how we're going to rebound."

Then, to have a pick at the plus-10 and give the offense a short field was big for us. It set up back-to-back drives when we stopped them on downs going into halftime.

That was a big momentum shift. We talk a lot about momentum in college football. Everybody talks about, "This is a key stat. This is a key stat." But if you look at the key indicators, they're all momentum plays.

If you win the explosive-play battle, what are explosive plays? They're big momentum swings. If you win the turnover battle, what is a turnover? It's momentum.

Especially when you're dealing with 18- to 22-year-olds, depending on what team you are, they might be older than that. Then you have the emotional roller coaster of it all.

How have Florida's four former Baylor defenders helped the unit?

I'm really impressed with the maturity level of those guys. I say it's not a surprise.

It's no different than when certain guys come from a certain high school and you know how they were raised and coached coming out of that program.

I know Coach Aranda really well and how he's developed from way back during his time at Wisconsin , LSU and before. We see things a lot of the same way in terms of how you develop a football player.

So much of it is awareness. That's why we harp so much on football IQ here. It's not about the X's and O's. The athleticism and strength are great. You need that, but smart, intelligent football players make football plays.

They do things that maybe super-athletic guys who aren't football-aware can't do. They play a step faster and read the formation. Where those guys came from would be why I think they've been such quality contributors.

What does Alfonzo Allen Jr. provide in the secondary?

He's a ball guy. He loves ball. He's super versatile in terms of being able to play at STAR or either safety position.

Again, we always say, "The more you can do," and he can do a lot for us. That's a huge skill set for us and allows us to have some flexibility in our rotations.

Certain defenses will call for certain guys. It's important as a play-caller that you try to highlight each player's skill set because his skill set is a little bit different than, say, Kanye's.

But you feel his physicality when he comes downhill and puts his hands on blockers. His block destruction is really good, and his tackling is firm and solid. He's been a really pleasant surprise for us.

What did you think of Kanye Clark's performance against FAU?

I thought there were some good things and some things that we need to work on. There were two different slot fades. One was obviously a really good play down there in the red zone. Then there was the one on third-and-long after the review and incomplete. We were bringing pressure. The quarterback saw it and just threw it up with Jaden Robinson barreling down on him. It was a good throw and catch.

If you're going to play Cover 1 at times, those are the hard ones. There's a reason that's the go-to shot when you know it's single-high or zero. You throw that all day long. You want to win more than you lose. He just happened to have two of those plays. It was a true 50-50.

When we accumulate it at the end of the season, you can ask me. If that thing looks like it's 65% or 70% in our favor, then he did a good job. If it stays 50-50, then we'll have a different discussion.

How do you teach the players to improve their situational awareness?

You try to find anything. You highlight it, but we talked about the touching-the-stove piece. You can talk until you're blue in the face, but a lot of these guys have to experience it.

The reality is that all of us tend to learn better when there's a consequence. Specifically, already this week, I'll stop a drill and say, "OK, what was the down and distance? What was the personnel?" I'll ask, and if they don't know everything about it, the whole defense is doing three up-downs. It's forcing them to think and forcing them to be overly aware in practice.

If they're not, it's not just them doing it. They're accountable to all their teammates. Trust me, when you start doing too many of them, everybody's going to be looking at you and telling you to make sure you know. Then it gets communicated across.

It's not just an individual issue. If I'm a safety and see my corner out there not pressed, I'm yelling at him to get down. It's not, "Well, I hope he gets down. That might be a minus on his play." Talk. Help each other. It's OK to help each other.

We're going to have some of those mechanics going forward. Again, that's on me. I probably should have been doing that more early. Sometimes you take some things for granted.

articles.title: Buccaneers news: Insider reveals how Baker Mayfield's extension came together
articles.summary: With the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Baker Mayfield agreeing on a $165 million contract extension, it resolves a long-standing affair that consisted of endless...
articles.body:
With the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Baker Mayfield agreeing on a $165 million contract extension, it resolves a long-standing affair that consisted of endless negotiations throughout the offseason. As the contract talks between the Buccaneers and Mayfield appeared to be dead at one point, this NFL insider gives insight into how everything unfolded.

While Mayfield and Tampa Bay agreed on a three-year extension worth $165 million, last Tuesday saw general manager Jason Richt implying that talks had halted and the focus was on the opener against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday. However, Mike Garafolo spoke on the NFL Network and expressed that he heard talks progressing back during the team's preseason finale against the New York Jets on Aug. 14.

"I'm on the field before the Buccaneers-Jets game, and I'm talking to a high-ranking Buccaneer source who says, 'We weren't that far away and, even the fact that you thought he didn't want a two-year deal, they countered to us with a two-year deal, so they were open to a shorter-term deal,' Wound up being a three-year deal," Garafolo said.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"So I pick up the phone, and I call my friend Ian Rapaport," Garafolo continued. "And I go, 'Hey, just so you know, this is going to get done before the season. Let's not sleep on this one.' So we continued to check, and all of a sudden you start to get the feel that it was real…and it may happen, and then it wound up happening here, and the fact that it stayed quiet the whole way, even though it was really when it came down to the negotiations only a couple of days."

At any rate, with the contract situation out of the way, all eyes are on Sunday in the Week 1 opener against the Bengals.

articles.title: Burnley boss confirms huge injury blow after Wrexham draw and provides updates on others
articles.summary: Burnley midfielder Hannibal is set to be sidelined for at least three to four months after undergoing surgery on a hamstring injury, Nicky Hayen has confirme...
articles.body:
Burnley midfielder Hannibal is set to be sidelined for at least three to four months after undergoing surgery on a hamstring injury, Nicky Hayen has confirmed.

Hannibal missed the Clarets' 1-1 draw with Wrexham after suffering the problem against Bristol City.

"Hannibal had his surgery today, so it will be at least three to four months that he will be out," Hayen told the Burnley Express .

Jordan Beyer , Bashir Humphreys , Josh Cullen , Enock Agyei , Jaydon Banel , Dastan Satpayev and Ashley Barnes are also currently unavailable.

Jacob Bruun Larsen missed the draw at Wrexham with a heel problem, although Hayen is hopeful his absence will be considerably shorter.

"This will be quite okay," he said. "I think it's under his heel that he feels some pain.

"He tried yesterday, but I don't think it will be a long injury.

"But again, it's an injury, another injury, and again this is the situation we're in and it's not an excuse, it's a reason."

Anel Ahmedhodzic was also due to start against Wrexham before illness forced a late change.

"Anel was sick," Hayen explained. "He was on the bench, but actually he started, but he was sick, so everything comes together and that's very unfortunate."

articles.title: Letting Myles Turner Walk Was Best Decision Pacers Ever Made
articles.summary: Losing Myles Turner looked tough at first, but in the end, it was one of the best moves by the Indiana Pacers.
articles.body:
After reaching the 2025 NBA Finals, the Indiana Pacers entered an offseason filled with all sorts of questions.

The biggest for them was whether the team would re-sign star center Myles Turner . After all, Turner had been one of the catalysts for the organization for many years, and there was all sorts of speculation that he would return.

So when Turner signed a massive four-year, $108.9 million contract with the Milwaukee Bucks , it came as a surprise to many people. But it was due to Turner feeling disrespected by the Pacers in negotiations.

Indiana had some hesitancy to hand him a large contract, even with all the success that he had seen with the franchise. And as it turns out, this was the correct move by the Pacers.

Turner's first season with the Bucks was nothing short of a disaster. The veteran big man put up the lowest points, rebounds, and blocks per game since his rookie season.

Overall, Turner averaged 11.9 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.5 assists, and 1.6 blocks per game, seeing 71 games on the court. This could have been due to him being in a new system, but Turner's play didn't justify the large contract he had signed.

Indiana dodged a bullet by lowballing Turner, but they may have seen something that nobody else did. There was a reason why the franchise didn't just easily hand Turner the money, especially after a run to the NBA Finals.

Turner could have a great second season with the Bucks, but he isn't getting any younger, with him now being 30-years-old. Milwaukee is also entering into somewhat of a rebuild, and after years of underperforming with the Pacers on the court, Turner may not be willing to stick around for that.

Indiana didn't immediately replace Turner last offseason, choosing to enter the season without a long-term answer. But the team did trade for Ivica Zubac , giving them a top option for the upcoming season.

Somehow, the Pacers still got something of value for Turner, even if it was not paying him over $25 million a season. Losing a player who meant so much to the franchise was tough, but the Pacers made the correct decision.

While at the time, the decision to allow Turner to walk was a big risk, it turned out to be the best move that the franchise could have made. The Pacers will enter the new 2026-27 season with renewed hope for a title run , and getting star guard Tyrese Haliburton back from injury should help everything.

articles.title: Know Your Enemy: Up-And-Coming Canadiens Could Be Sabres' Toughest Atlantic Division Rival
articles.summary: As part of an ongoing series here on TheHockeyNews.com, we're breaking down each of the Buffalo Sabres' Eastern Conference opponents. And in this file, we're...
articles.body:
The Buffalo Sabres ' 2025-26 season was largely a major success, as the Sabres finished first in the Atlantic Division, then beat the Boston Bruins in their first-round Stanley Cup playoff series. However, the Sabres lost to the Montreal Canadiens in the second round. Still, Buffalo ended their decade-and-a-half playoff drought, and that was a huge relief for long-suffering Sabres fans.

Meanwhile, for the second straight year here at TheHockeyNews.com , we're analyzing the Sabres' Eastern Conference opponents in an online series titled "Know Your Enemy". And in this particular file in the series, we're breaking down that Canadiens team.

The Habs didn't make many moves this summer, but they've been expertly-constructed by GM Kent Hughes, and if the Sabres are to improve in 2026-27, they'll need to go through the Canadiens.

NEW CANADIENS PLAYERS: Brett Berard (LW), Sasha Pastujov (LW)

2025-26 SERIES: Sabres 2-2-0, Canadiens 2-2-0

2026-27 GAMES AGAINST EACH OTHER: October 13, at Montreal; October 17 at Montreal; December 18 at Buffalo; January 18 at Buffalo

CAN THE SABRES BEAT THIS TEAM? The Sabres will take on the Canadiens in Montreal in Buffalo's seventh game of the regular-season – and in a quirk of the schedule, the Sabres will play the Habs four days later, again in Montreal. That should get the two teams plenty-accustomed to one another, and from that point, Buffalo will host the Canadiens twice in a one-month period that ends in mid-January.

The Sabres and Canadiens split their series last season, with both teams winning twice in regulation. And if we're being honest, we can see that same type of result taking place in 2026-27. Montreal hasn't made any material changes to their roster, but Hughes has done a masterful job of putting the Habs together, and the Sabres will have to be at their best to even have a chance of beating the Canadiens this coming year.

The Canadiens sent Buffalo home for the summer this past spring, and to avoid that fate in '26-27, the Sabres will need to be better than Montreal in the goaltending department, and there's obviously no guarantee that will take place. But Buffalo has lost key pieces Alex Tuch and Bowen Byram , and unless the Sabres get internal improvement from their young players, beating the Habs will require a huge step forward for Buffalo.

Can the Sabres turn the tables on Montreal this year? Yes, there's definitely a chance they can do so. However, if the Canadiens wind up dumping Buffalo for the second straight season, you have to think Sabres GM Jarmo Kekalainen will be much more active on the trade and free-agency fronts next summer.

There's lots to like about both Buffalo and the Habs, but one of those teams will be seriously disappointed by an early exit in the 2027 playoffs.

And unless the Sabres can avoid doing so, getting eliminated by Montreal for the second straight season will almost assuredly lead to Buffalo's roster being thoroughly overhauled for the 2027-28 campaign.
